_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for AVGO retrospectives (retro/build_avgo.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern); every release came after the close except Q2 FY15's (before the open; its full text, with the financial statements, in an 8-K/A after the close that day) and Q2 FY22's (before the open on 2022-05-26, with the VMware announcement). 'splits' holds the 10-for-1 split effective 2024-07-15: from that day every per-share fact published before it is divided by 10 and every share count multiplied (on_basis); a vintage year taken from a 10-K published before the split keeps that 10-K's date ('eps_published', 'shares_published'). Avago Technologies Limited listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on 2009-08-06 (its first trading day in the price data); before that it filed only as the issuer of notes (Avago Technologies Finance Pte. Ltd.: 20-F and 6-K), so the series starts at the listing and the P/E window runs from it; from 2016-02-02 the listed company is Broadcom Limited, its successor issuer, and from 2018-04-05 Broadcom Inc., redomiciled in Delaware ('company_names'). The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF (the IPO prospectus, then each 10-K), the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the latest next-quarter revenue guide for the quarter after the latest print, and events published since that vintage. Avago's fiscal year ended on October 31 to FY2007 and from FY2008 on the Sunday closest to October 31. Values are as reported, per share on the basis of the filing that published them. A print keeps its raw published figures ('raw', $M) and the margins, growth and gaps derived from them; the builder re-derives and checks them. 'eps_first_excluded' holds the first years left out of the history (losses); 'eps_excluded' later years left out (losses, or a distorted year whose listed one-off items exceed its income: FY2014; or whose listed one-off benefits exceed its income without them, the mirror test: FY2018). Each guide states the next quarter's revenue as growth on the quarter just reported ('seq_pct'); 'level_m' is that growth applied to the reported quarter and 'yoy_pct' the level against the same quarter a year earlier from its own release (the input); a guide stated as a dollar level or range ('level_stated': the 8-K of 2010-08-10, and the releases from Q2 FY14) is read against that quarter directly; its other lines ('display') feed nothing. From the Q4 FY18 release Broadcom guided the fiscal year: a guide with 'period' is a dollar level read against the previous fiscal year's net revenue, used when no next-quarter guide is in scope (method r2's fallback), and 'op_margin_guide_pct' is its GAAP operating margin as a level (FY2019), the guided margin step; 'withdrawn' voids every earlier guide for its year (FY2020, 2020-03-13). From the Q4 FY23 release Broadcom again guided the fiscal year only (FY2024, including VMware, acquired on 2023-11-22), and from the Q3 FY24 release the next quarter again. FY2024 is excluded as a distorted year (its one-time tax provision and VMware items exceed its income from continuing operations), as FY2014 was. Quarter guides that 8-Ks gave only as non-GAAP net revenue (2018-01-31, 2018-04-30) are taken as published, the latest guide for a quarter winning; a guide restated only in words keeps the last numeric range in a record of its own (2017-11-02). From FY2010 the releases' balance sheets no longer carry the year-ago quarter, so a print's year-ago inventory comes from that quarter's own release ('extra_sources'). 'dividends' hold each declared quarterly rate from the first filing that states it (the first, $0.07, with the Q4 FY10 results). 'events' hold dated theme evidence (CLOUD, company-acknowledged in each 10-K from FY2016). 'fiscal_calendar' lists the 53-week years whose year end differs from the Sunday closest to October 31 (FY2018, ended November 4, 2018). rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

rule_t._doc: Rule T over the years the filings report: AVGO listed on 2009-08-06, and its filings published by then report FY2004-FY2008 (FY2004-FY2005 the Predecessor) for the statement of operations and three year-end inventory changes, so each signal has four annual values (three for the inventory gap), not ten. The formula is the LOW/NKE one: XBULL = the best year, BULL = the median, BASE = the worst year, BEAR = one median-to-worst step beyond the worst (mirrored where lower is better); rounded half up to whole percent or points and to 10 bp. Each change comes from the latest filing published by 2009-08-07 that reports both years; FY2006 is the company's published combined year (one Predecessor month and eleven Company months, $1,513M). GAAP as reported: no filing publishes gross or operating margin excluding only the FY2007 asset impairment, and the FY2004 and FY2005 revenue keep the Camera Module Business ($296M and $69M) as published.
